newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ATLETICO WITHOUT CAMINERO FOR CRUNCH GAME WITH BETIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO WITHOUT CAMINERO FOR CRUNCH GAME WITH BETIS.

text.p: Atletico Madrid coach Radomir Antic must have been hoping that Saturday's game against Real Betis would be less controversial than last season's encounters between the two sides.
But even before the Spanish championship clash has begun the Serbian has been landed with a row he could have done without.

International playmaker Jose Luis Caminero, who joined the Spanish squad last week with a minor leg strain, returned with a more serious muscle injury that will keep him out of action for around a month.
He did not even play against the Czech Republic.
"I was surprised to see him on the substitute's bench," said Antic, who has a history of conflict with Spanish manager Javier Clemente.
Several Spanish clubs have been angered by Clemente's uncompromising approach and are increasingly unwilling to let players join the national side.
Last season, it was not only players who were injured in the Betis-Atletico cup tie.
A locker room door was smashed -- apparently by Atletico players -- after a dramatic game which ended with an Atletico official making death-threats to Betis manager Lorenzo Serra Ferrer.

Match officials and several players were hit by missiles thrown by fans angered by some dubious refereeing, including a decision not to send off Atletico keeper Jose Molina for handball outside the area after just three minutes.
In retrospect it could easily have been a turning point in Atletico's most memorable season, but Antic's men overcame the furore and went on to complete the club's first-ever double.
After six games champions Atletico trail leaders Real Madrid and Barcelona by four points and their scintillating form in Europe has contrasted with some ordinary performances at home.
Betis have started strongly thanks to Alfonso Perez and Nigerian strike partner George Finidi. With three straight wins and not a goal let in away from home they are riding high in third place.
Key defender Hristo Vidakovic is back from playing for Yugoslavia in the Faroes, but the southerners also have their problems.
Serra Ferrer is currently organising his defence after being charged with assaulting a police officer who was giving him a parking ticket.
If found guilty Serra Ferrer could be sentenced to a year in jail.
